fourthdimension.ponder.matching.header: Match the car to its functional track
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_1: Each 4D family needs its own matching track. The colored strips here are route diagrams.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_2: Arrow, Legacy ZacSpin, Free Spin, Revised Free-Rotor and PAX are separate mechanisms.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_3: An appearance style changes decoration. It does not turn ordinary track into 4D track.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_4: Only verified fitting ordinary adapters can use the main rails. They receive no 4D seat effects.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_5: Keep disabled 4D cars on matching track. Ordinary rail access does not certify recovery towing.
fourthdimension.ponder.construction.head: Connect anchors and assemble a matching car
fourthdimension.ponder.construction.text: Place native Coasters anchors. Use the family track item on the first anchor, then the second.
Sneak-click with the track item to cancel a selection. Continue the route with the same family.
These colored blocks illustrate a route; they are not track blocks to place. Shape the real connection with native Coasters tools.
Use the matching car item on a connected anchor. Clear the whole rotating seat and rider corridor.
Use the Rotation Tool on an anchor to edit its section. Rebind profiles after changing track geometry.
The chassis needs propulsion from Create or the native chain system. Seat rotation does not drive the train.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_1: The Arrow car has four seats on two driven wing carriers. It requires Controlled 4D Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_2: This is a motion diagram. In the ride, paired followers read the control rails; a rack and 8:1 gear train drive the real carrier axle.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_3: The car follows the profile on its bound section. Edit that section's keys as distance:degrees[:slope], separated by semicolons.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_4: Keep a full turn as 360 degrees, not zero. Place the car on the section with the profile you authored.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_5: The exposed spring allows limited tracking lag. During capture or acquisition the clutch opens, so a non-neutral rail does not pretend to drive a neutral seat.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_6: Capture and align both carriers before boarding. Close restraints before releasing capture and dispatching; the clutch re-engages after the axle acquires its target.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_7: If tracking exceeds the spring travel, the clutch releases and the train requests stop and capture. Inspect the profile and fault before resuming.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_1: The Legacy ZacSpin car has eight seats on two back-to-back carriers. Use Legacy ZacSpin Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_2: Gravity, track motion and rider loading drive its free rotation. Section angle keys do not drive these carriers.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_3: The groups can respond differently. Use the Rotation Tool on the car to tune damping and ballast.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_4: This diagram illustrates free motion; it is not a prediction of a particular ride's spin.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_5: Request capture, then wait for both carriers to align and stop before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.header: Four independently rotating Free Spin pairs
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_1: The Free Spin car has eight seats in four paired carriers. It requires Magnetic Free Spin Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_2: Each group has its own free hinge. Rider loading and motion can give the groups different responses.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_3: Matching track accepts magnetic spans. Inducers add torque; dampers oppose angular velocity.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_4: Select span targets with the Rotation Tool. The animation is an illustration, not an exact manufacturer coupling model.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_5: Damping is not a boarding lock. Capture all four carriers and wait for readiness before unloading.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_1: The Revised Free-Rotor car has eight seats in four independent pairs. Use Revised Free-Rotor Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_2: Its lower hinges and chassis differ from the Free Spin car. They need their own matching mechanism and clearance.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_3: Tune damping and ballast on the car. Section rotation keys do not drive its free carriers.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_4: Compare the groups under different rider loading. This is an original inspired variant, not exact manufacturer coupling.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_5: Stop the chassis, capture every group and wait for alignment before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.header: Induce spin, damp spin, then capture
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_1: Use an Inducer or Damper on a Magnetic Free Spin section to install a span.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_2: Edit its start and end distances, direction, strength, falloff and target mask with the Rotation Tool.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_3: Orange marks an inducer. Track-mounted magnetic faces act across an air gap on the selected carriers’ reaction rings.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_4: Cyan marks a damper. It opposes existing spin across the same air gap; it does not prescribe a final seat angle or mechanically latch the carrier.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_5: Targets use car-local left-front 1, left-rear 2, right-front 4, right-rear 8. Add them; 15 selects all four.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_6: Rollback does not swap these group names. Ordinary carts receive no magnetic seat assistance.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_7: Capture and readiness provide the boarding lock. A slow carrier is not automatically safe to board.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_1: Use an empty hand on the Boarding Station to bind a nearby non-PAX car. The station does not propel it.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_2: Power at the rear requests capture. Wait for a stopped chassis, aligned carriers and the front readiness signal.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_3: Board an open seat with empty hands. Use the Rotation Tool on the car to close restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_4: The right indicator reports closed restraints. Keep capture until riders are secured.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_5: Remove rear power to request dispatch. Restraints must be closed; the propulsion system moves the car.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_6: On return, request capture and wait for readiness before opening restraints and unloading onto a platform.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_7: PAX uses the winch cycle instead. Its return capture must complete before boarding or unloading.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.header: PAX catch, powered lift, release and return
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_1: Build one connected PAX track route between two spikes. The compact route shown here is a diagram.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_2: Place four PAX cars six blocks apart. Hold a Minecraft Chain, right-click one car then its neighbor, and repeat for each adjacent pair.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_3: Place a winch within twelve blocks of the stopped train. Sneak-use it to bind, then supply Create rotation at 16 to 128 RPM. This is the remote drive unit.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_4: Wait for boarding readiness. Board, close restraints and have the platform operator use the winch to start.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_5: A separate guided carriage engages the lead receiver and lifts the train. At the crest its catch releases; the train then travels freely.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_6: The shuttle passes outbound, reverses and returns. Seat rotation remains free during the ride.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_7: The returning train is caught and retained. Wait for the winch to report boarding readiness before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_8: If lift power is interrupted, restore power, inspect the route and use the winch normally to resume. The diagram does not show a cable to the remote drive.
